sourceOfTruth: docs/v01 bilingual v0.1 final user manual

scenarios.name: database batch run
scenarios.trigger: authenticated business request selects a finite database dataset
scenarios.config: definition, inputSchema, keyset source, mapper, pageSize, sequential dispatch
scenarios.execute: start one durable BatchRun and let Coordinator page until exhaustion
scenarios.expectedState: all persisted batches cross execution and completion barriers before final completion
scenarios.failure: source, mapper, dispatch, processor, completion, or Redis interruption
scenarios.recovery: resume, recovery run, completion retry, or fresh run according to failure class
scenarios.observe: run cursors, batch summaries, worker identities, completion state, business audit
scenarios.executableEvidence: canonical workflow and implementation acceptance contract

scenarios.name: direct job
scenarios.trigger: authenticated request already contains one bounded executable payload
scenarios.expectedState: 202 plus durable job identity and one idempotent business result
scenarios.failure: Redis unavailable, identity conflict, backpressure, or processor failure
scenarios.recovery: same-identity retry or failed direct-job replacement
scenarios.observe: job state, attempt, generation, and business state
scenarios.executableEvidence: bilingual API recipe and inspect path

scenarios.name: paced batches and dual cursors
scenarios.trigger: bounded overlap is required for throughput
scenarios.execute: dispatch later batches while earlier barriers remain pending
scenarios.expectedState: dispatchCursor may lead checkpointCursor without skipping a barrier gap
scenarios.recovery: rebuild from persisted batches and cascade checkpoint only across contiguous barriers
scenarios.observe: both cursors, in-flight batches, hold reason, completion states

scenarios.name: distributed workers
scenarios.config: shared Redis/namespace/queue, per-process concurrency, lease and drain
scenarios.execute: multiple Workers atomically claim the same queue
scenarios.expectedState: one current generation per active job and bounded aggregate concurrency
scenarios.failure: Worker crash, renewal uncertainty, stale settlement, or downstream saturation
scenarios.recovery: stalled reclaim, fencing, controlled scale, and idempotent downstream
scenarios.observe: heartbeats, worker IDs, active jobs, generations, waiting age
scenarios.executableEvidence: topology, crash sequence, drain and rollout procedure

scenarios.name: delay and retry
scenarios.trigger: future due time or retryable processor failure
scenarios.config: delayMs, attempts, timeoutMs, exponential backoff, jitter
scenarios.execute: cooperative owner promotes due work and Worker executes attempts
scenarios.expectedState: delayed/retrying becomes waiting and eventually completed or failed
scenarios.failure: no time owner, timeout, non-retryable error, or exhausted budget
scenarios.recovery: restore eligible Worker, repair cause, or create correct replacement
scenarios.observe: state, due time, attempt, stalledRecoveries, owner

scenarios.name: business idempotency
scenarios.config: stable business idempotency key and provider/state-machine/outbox boundary
scenarios.execute: redeliver after downstream success and ACK loss using the same key
scenarios.expectedState: one user-visible effect and current-generation settlement
scenarios.failure: random key, uncertain timeout, or queue dedup used as business truth
scenarios.recovery: query provider/business state and retry only with the original key
scenarios.observe: job/run identity, attempt, generation, business key, provider result ID
scenarios.executableEvidence: three production patterns and ACK-loss acceptance drill

scenarios.name: batch and run completion delivery
scenarios.trigger: a Batch or Run reaches execution terminal state
scenarios.config: named completion handlers, attempts, timeout, backoff
scenarios.execute: persist, claim, deliver, and settle a completion event
scenarios.expectedState: barrier passes only at not_required or delivered
scenarios.failure: handler timeout, downstream error, exhausted delivery attempts, or stale owner
scenarios.recovery: repair handler and retry the exact event without redoing jobs
scenarios.observe: event ID/type, delivery attempt/generation, execution and completion states
scenarios.executableEvidence: dual-state diagram, idempotent handler, and CLI recovery

scenarios.name: blocked run resume
scenarios.trigger: Source/Dispatch retries exhaust or Redis recovery precondition fails
scenarios.config: source/dispatch retry policy and strict Redis policy
scenarios.execute: repair cause and resume the same non-terminal Run
scenarios.expectedState: same identity continues from persisted boundary and cursors
scenarios.failure: state lost, cursor mismatch, unsafe role, or incompatible source
scenarios.recovery: restore safety or choose backup/fresh Run instead of retryFailed
scenarios.observe: executionState, boundary, both cursors, dispatchHoldReason, generation, Redis role, failure list
scenarios.executableEvidence: resume precondition checklist and fail-safe contract

scenarios.name: recovery run
scenarios.trigger: terminal mapper or processor failures have retained replay envelopes
scenarios.config: retention, definition compatibility, recovery idempotency key
scenarios.execute: runs.retryFailed creates a new Run from stable failure sequence
scenarios.expectedState: new recovery identity replays only failed work and preserves original Run
scenarios.failure: expired envelope, unavailable definition, or changed-data intent
scenarios.recovery: restore compatible runtime or start a fresh business-data Run
scenarios.observe: parentRunId, recoveryDepth, stage, envelope expiry, summaries
scenarios.executableEvidence: CLI procedure and failure decision table

scenarios.name: production Redis topology
scenarios.config: Redis >=7.2, noeviction, persistence, ACL/TLS, strict policy, single primary
scenarios.execute: start roles in dependency order and run readiness preflight
scenarios.expectedState: one writable primary, safe role readiness, durable work within declared RPO
scenarios.failure: policy error, persistence error, split brain, or acknowledged write loss
scenarios.recovery: stop new work, restore Redis or accept loss window and start fresh business Runs
scenarios.observe: server info, persistence, replication, health, config digest
scenarios.executableEvidence: topology, commands, startup order, and production drill list

scenarios.name: vext integration
scenarios.trigger: authenticated vext route starts Queuebit work
scenarios.config: native plugin, app extension, client lifecycle, independent role commands
scenarios.execute: derive tenant server-side, start Run, and return 202
scenarios.expectedState: one long-lived Web client and independent durable background roles
scenarios.failure: unauthorized access, invalid input, identity conflict, backpressure, or Redis unready
scenarios.observe: runId, deduplicated, states, role readiness, tenant audit
scenarios.executableEvidence: vextjs@0.3.26 plugin and route target contract

scenarios.name: operational diagnosis
scenarios.trigger: queue latency, errors, or safety signals change
scenarios.config: metrics, health stale threshold, backpressure watermarks, log correlation
scenarios.execute: inspect queue, Workers, Coordinator, and health before acting
scenarios.expectedState: operator distinguishes busy, slow, stuck, and unsafe states
scenarios.failure: single-process metric treated as cluster total or arbitrary threshold creates false action
scenarios.recovery: use SLO/load-test thresholds and follow symptom-specific runbook
scenarios.observe: waiting age, states, cursors, leases, completion, Redis policy
scenarios.executableEvidence: four-view workflow, capacity formulas, alert and drain tables
